questions.stem: A team needs a custom Kubernetes operator (CRD) and direct control of the node pool for a specialized scheduler. Which requirement most clearly rules out Azure Container Apps?
options: The requirement for a custom CRD-based operator and node-level control
The desire to run Linux containers
The use of environment variables for configuration
questions.explanation: Azure Container Apps abstracts the Kubernetes control plane, so custom operators/CRDs and node-level control are not exposed. That is a genuine constraint favoring AKS.

questions.stem: Which Azure service is purpose-built for serverless containers with built-in scale-to-zero, HTTP ingress, and event-driven scaling without managing Kubernetes?
questions.explanation: Azure Container Apps provides serverless containers with KEDA-based event scaling, scale-to-zero, and managed ingress on top of a hidden Kubernetes and Dapr/KEDA/Envoy foundation.

questions.stem: A workload requires Windows containers. What is the correct Container Apps conclusion?
options: Enable a Windows workload profile in the environment
Windows containers are not supported; select another service such as AKS or App Service
Convert the environment to Consumption-only mode
Use a Dedicated profile to unlock Windows support
questions.explanation: Azure Container Apps runs Linux containers only. A hard Windows-container requirement is an exit trigger toward AKS or App Service.

questions.stem: Which unit in Azure Container Apps is the deployable application boundary that owns ingress and revisions?
questions.explanation: A container app is the application boundary that owns its ingress configuration and produces revisions; the environment is the shared secure boundary that hosts multiple apps.

questions.stem: A batch of records must be processed on a schedule and then the compute should stop entirely. Which Container Apps construct fits best?
options: A container app with min replicas set to 1
An external ingress app with a timer sidecar
questions.explanation: Container Apps jobs run to completion on a schedule or event and then stop, which suits scheduled or finite work better than an always-considered app.

questions.stem: A platform team is creating a new environment that needs Consumption and Dedicated profiles plus UDR support. Which environment type should it choose?
questions.explanation: The workload profiles environment is the default and supports Consumption, Dedicated, and Flex (preview) profiles plus richer networking. Consumption-only is the legacy structure.

questions.stem: A bursty service must incur no replica compute charge while idle. In a workload profiles environment, which profile type can scale to zero?
options: All profile types scale to zero identically
questions.explanation: The Consumption profile can scale to zero. Dedicated bills per running instance, and the Flex profile (preview) cannot scale to zero.

questions.stem: A release engineer asks to edit an existing revision in place after deployment. Which statement explains why that plan is invalid?
options: It is mutable and can be edited in place
It is an immutable snapshot of a specific app configuration and container image
It only exists in single-revision mode
It stores durable application data for replicas
questions.explanation: A revision is an immutable snapshot. Changing revision-scope properties creates a new revision rather than mutating the existing one.

questions.stem: An app writes uploaded files to the container filesystem and expects them to persist across replica restarts. What is the flaw?
options: The container filesystem is durable, so there is no flaw
Replica local storage is ephemeral; durable data needs external storage such as Azure Files or Blob
Files persist only if min replicas is greater than one
Files persist only in Dedicated profiles
questions.explanation: Replica-local storage is ephemeral. Durable data must go to external storage, and shared state needs an Azure Files volume mount or an external service.

questions.stem: Which probe removes a replica from receiving traffic when it fails, without restarting the replica?
questions.explanation: A failing readiness probe gates traffic away from the replica. A failing liveness probe restarts the replica; a startup probe tolerates slow initialization.

questions.stem: To pull an image from Azure Container Registry using managed identity, which role must the identity hold on the registry?
questions.explanation: AcrPull grants image pull rights. Assign it to the app's managed identity at the registry scope to avoid registry credentials.

questions.stem: You need an app to read a secret from Key Vault using managed identity with least privilege. Which role should you grant?
questions.explanation: Key Vault Secrets User grants read access to secret values under RBAC, which satisfies least privilege for retrieval without write or management rights.

questions.stem: A create-time Key Vault secret reference fails because the identity does not yet exist. What is the most likely cause?
options: Key Vault does not support Container Apps
A system-assigned identity does not exist until its app is created, so it cannot be granted access beforehand
The vault must be in a different region
AcrPull was assigned instead of a secrets role
questions.explanation: A system-assigned identity is created with the app, so it cannot be granted vault access before the app exists. A user-assigned identity created first avoids the chicken-and-egg problem.

questions.stem: Which statement about private endpoints on a Container Apps environment is correct?
options: They require public network access to remain enabled
They require public network access to be disabled and incur additional charges
They are free and enabled by default
They are only available in Consumption-only environments
questions.explanation: Using a private endpoint requires public network access to be disabled on the environment and incurs private endpoint charges.

questions.stem: An internal-only environment resolves a private DNS name but connections still fail. What does this most directly indicate?
options: DNS resolution and network reachability are separate; a route, NSG, or firewall is likely blocking the path
The app must be redeployed to a Dedicated profile
Private DNS is not supported for internal environments
questions.explanation: A DNS answer proves name resolution, not reachability. Failing connections after a good DNS answer point to routing, NSG, or firewall controls on the path.

questions.stem: For a workload profiles (v2) environment injected into a custom VNet, what is the documented minimum subnet size?
questions.explanation: A workload profiles environment requires a dedicated subnet of at least /27. The legacy Consumption-only environment requires /23.

questions.stem: You must give a workload a single stable outbound public IP for a partner allowlist. Which control fits best?
options: Assign a public IP to each replica
Associate a NAT Gateway with the environment subnet
questions.explanation: A NAT Gateway on the subnet gives a predictable, stable outbound IP for egress, which suits partner allowlists. Azure Firewall adds inspection when required.

questions.stem: Which technology powers event-driven autoscaling in Azure Container Apps?
questions.explanation: Container Apps uses KEDA to scale on HTTP, TCP, CPU, memory, and many event sources such as queues.

questions.stem: An HTTP app is set to min replicas 0. Users report occasional slow first requests. What is the most accurate explanation?
options: Scale-to-zero is broken and must be disabled
Cold start latency occurs when scaling from zero; set a minimum replica count if the latency SLO cannot absorb it
The Dedicated profile is required for all HTTP apps
questions.explanation: Scaling from zero adds cold-start latency. If the SLO cannot absorb it, keep a minimum replica warm; otherwise scale-to-zero is a valid cost tradeoff.

questions.stem: A queue worker scales up aggressively and the downstream database begins throttling. What is the sound corrective principle?
options: Increase max replicas further to overcome throttling
Bound max replicas to the safe downstream concurrency the dependency can absorb
questions.explanation: More replicas amplify pressure on a throttled dependency. Scale to the bottleneck by bounding max replicas to safe downstream concurrency.

questions.stem: When must zone redundancy be configured for a Container Apps environment?
options: Any time after creation via an update
At environment creation time; it cannot be changed afterward
questions.explanation: Zone redundancy is set at environment creation and is immutable. To change it, create a new environment.

questions.stem: For a 99.9% monthly availability SLO, approximately how much downtime is the error budget?
questions.explanation: 99.9% over 30 days allows roughly 43.2 minutes of budgeted downtime, which drives burn-rate alerting.

questions.stem: A worker uses at-least-once messaging and a replica is killed mid-message. What must the design guarantee?
options: Idempotent, duplicate-safe processing because the message can be redelivered
The message is lost and should be ignored
Ingress must be disabled to prevent duplicates
questions.explanation: At-least-once delivery means a message can be redelivered after a failure, so processing must be idempotent and duplicate-safe.

questions.stem: In multiple revision mode, how is production traffic distributed between revisions?
options: By explicit traffic weights that total 100
questions.explanation: Traffic splitting uses explicit weights across active revisions that must total 100, enabling canary and blue-green patterns.

questions.stem: A canary at 10% shows elevated errors on the candidate revision. What is the fastest safe rollback?
options: Shift traffic weight back to the previous known-good revision
questions.explanation: Because revisions are retained, rollback is a traffic-weight change to the known-good revision, completing in seconds to minutes without rebuilding.

questions.stem: Where do Container Apps console and system logs land for KQL analysis by default?
options: To a Log Analytics workspace via the environment's logging configuration
questions.explanation: The environment sends console and system logs to a Log Analytics workspace where ContainerAppConsoleLogs and system tables can be queried with KQL.

questions.stem: You want distributed tracing across services in Container Apps. What is the accurate constraint?
options: The Application Insights auto-instrumentation agent is fully supported and enabled by default
The auto-instrumentation agent is not supported; instrument with the SDK or use the managed OpenTelemetry agent
Tracing is impossible in Container Apps
questions.explanation: Container Apps does not support the Application Insights auto-instrumentation agent; use SDK-based instrumentation or the managed OpenTelemetry agent.

questions.stem: What is required for an Azure Monitor alert to notify responders?
options: An action group attached to the alert rule
questions.explanation: Alert rules route notifications through an action group. Without one, the condition can fire but no one is notified.

questions.stem: How is the Consumption plan primarily billed in Container Apps?
options: A flat monthly fee per app
Per vCPU-second and GiB-second of active/idle usage plus HTTP requests, with monthly free grants
Per node in the underlying cluster
questions.explanation: Consumption bills resource allocation as vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds (active and idle rates) plus request charges, with monthly free grants.

questions.stem: A steady, high-utilization workload runs continuously with predictable demand. Which billing model is often more economical?
options: Dedicated workload profile, because sustained usage can be cheaper than per-second Consumption plus a management fee comparison
There is never a cost difference
questions.explanation: For sustained high utilization, a Dedicated profile (billed per instance plus a management fee) can undercut Consumption. The break-even depends on utilization.

questions.stem: Data residency rules require processing to stay within a specific geography. What is the primary architectural lever?
options: Region selection for the environment and its dependent data services
questions.explanation: Residency is governed primarily by choosing compliant regions for the environment and its data services; ACA resources are region-scoped.

questions.stem: Which practice most reduces log-related cost while keeping useful signal?
options: Apply sampling and scope queries to needed fields and windows
questions.explanation: Telemetry sampling and disciplined, scoped querying reduce ingestion and retention cost while preserving actionable signal.

questions.stem: A latency-sensitive public API must never cold-start during business hours but can save cost overnight. What is a defensible configuration?
options: A minimum replica floor during business hours and scale-to-zero permitted off-hours
Dedicated profile only, with no scaling
questions.explanation: Keeping a warm floor during peak hours protects the latency SLO while permitting scale-to-zero off-hours captures savings; the tradeoff is driven by the SLO.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Flex workload profile (preview) is accurate?
options: It scales to zero like Consumption
It requires a /25 subnet and cannot scale to zero
It is the legacy default profile
questions.explanation: The Flex profile (preview) requires a /25 subnet and cannot scale to zero, positioning it between Consumption and Dedicated.

questions.stem: A reviewer finds a database connection string committed in the repository for a Container App. Under the workshop rules, what is the impact?
options: It is acceptable if the repo is private
It is a critical failure; secrets must come from Key Vault or secret references, never source control
It is fine if the app also uses managed identity
questions.explanation: A committed credential is a critical failure. Secrets must be delivered via Key Vault references or app secrets and accessed with managed identity.

questions.stem: During a modeled zone failure, which outcome is expected for a zone-redundant environment?
options: No requests ever fail and no data is lost
Capacity survives the zone loss, though in-flight requests may fail and ephemeral data in the lost zone is gone
questions.explanation: Zone redundancy preserves capacity across a zone loss, but in-flight requests can fail and ephemeral data on lost replicas is gone. Durable state must be external and replicated.

questions.stem: You need a stable test URL for a candidate revision while production weights change. What feature helps?
options: Revision labels that provide stable per-revision URLs
questions.explanation: Revision labels give a stable URL to a specific revision for testing, independent of the traffic weights controlling production distribution.

questions.stem: What is the recommended way to protect a public Container Apps ingress from common web attacks?
options: Rely solely on the app code
Place Azure Front Door or Application Gateway with WAF in front of ingress
Use only NSGs on the subnet
questions.explanation: A WAF via Azure Front Door or Application Gateway in front of ingress protects against common web attacks and centralizes edge policy.

questions.stem: Which monthly free grants are associated with the Consumption plan (per subscription) at the documented level?
options: Roughly 180,000 vCPU-seconds, 360,000 GiB-seconds, and 2 million requests
questions.explanation: The Consumption plan includes documented monthly free grants of about 180,000 vCPU-seconds, 360,000 GiB-seconds, and 2 million requests.

questions.stem: A brownfield .NET app stores session state on the local disk of each instance. To move it to Container Apps, what change is required?
options: Nothing; local session works across replicas
Move session to a distributed store because replicas are stateless and interchangeable
Set min replicas to 1 to keep session
Use a Dedicated profile to persist local disk
questions.explanation: Replicas are ephemeral and interchangeable, so in-process/local session must move to a distributed cache or store before migration.

questions.stem: Which two properties define a scale rule's bounds in Container Apps?
options: CPU limit and memory limit only
questions.explanation: Scaling is bounded by minimum and maximum replica counts; the scale rule then decides where within those bounds to run.

questions.stem: An internal-facing worker should have no public exposure. Which ingress setting is correct?
questions.explanation: A background worker that nothing calls over HTTP should have ingress disabled; a private caller uses internal ingress. Never expose it externally.

questions.stem: You measure p95 latency well within SLO but p99 spikes during scale-out. What is a reasonable interpretation?
options: Cold-start or resource contention during scale events affects tail latency; consider warm floor or resource tuning
questions.explanation: Tail latency spikes during scale-out often reflect cold-start or contention. A warm minimum or resource tuning can protect p99 if the SLO demands it.

questions.stem: Why should container images be referenced by digest rather than a mutable tag for certification evidence?
options: A digest is immutable and guarantees the exact image, ensuring reproducibility
questions.explanation: A digest pins the exact image content, giving reproducible deployments; a mutable tag can change underneath you.

questions.stem: Leadership asks for cost per successful transaction. What must the cost model include beyond compute?
options: Requests, logs/telemetry, network egress, registry, storage, security, and edge services
questions.explanation: Total cost of ownership spans compute, requests, telemetry, network, registry, storage, security, and edge; unit economics require all of them.

questions.stem: Which alerting approach reduces false pages against an error budget?
options: A single static threshold on raw errors
Multi-window burn-rate alerts on the error budget
questions.explanation: Multi-window, multi-burn-rate alerts on the error budget catch fast and slow burns while suppressing noise from brief blips.

questions.stem: You must prove private access is actually enforced. Which evidence is sufficient?
options: A screenshot of the DNS zone
A public client that fails plus an approved private client that resolves the private address and succeeds
A note that ingress is internal
The app returns 200 from your laptop
questions.explanation: Enforcement is proven by a failing public attempt and a succeeding approved private attempt, combining resolution and reachability.

questions.stem: Which component provides the managed ingress and TLS termination inside a Container Apps environment?
options: Envoy-based ingress managed by the platform
questions.explanation: Container Apps uses an Envoy-based managed ingress for HTTP routing and TLS termination, abstracted from the user.

questions.stem: A scale-rule change was applied and a new revision appeared unexpectedly to a team. What should they have documented first?
options: Which properties are revision-scoped versus application-scoped before editing
questions.explanation: Knowing which changes are revision-scoped (create a new revision) versus application-scoped (apply in place) prevents surprise revisions during operations.

questions.stem: You right-size an app and cut CPU, but a re-run load test shows p99 regressing past SLO. What is the correct action?
options: Keep the saving; cost matters most
Reject the change because it regressed reliability/performance, and record the evidence
Increase min replicas to hide it
questions.explanation: A cost saving that regresses the SLO must be rejected and documented; validated savings only count when reliability and performance hold.

questions.stem: A team wants Functions triggers and bindings, but also needs to colocate event handlers with private APIs in an existing Container Apps environment and use its workload profiles. Which hosting choice best fits?
options: A generic container app with a hand-built polling loop
Azure Functions on the existing Container Apps environment using kind=functionapp
A scheduled Container Apps job for every message
A Windows Function App on the Consumption plan
questions.explanation: Native Functions on Container Apps preserves the Functions programming model while applying the environment's networking, observability, and workload-profile capabilities.

questions.stem: Which property distinguishes a native Functions workload from a generic Azure Container App when deployed by CLI or ARM?
questions.explanation: Native Functions support is selected with the functionapp kind; scale, ingress, and workload profile values are not unique to Functions.

questions.stem: A Service Bus-triggered Function on Container Apps never scales from zero even though messages accumulate. Ingress was disabled because the app has no public HTTP endpoint. What is the first platform-specific correction?
options: Add a manual CPU KEDA rule
Enable ingress, either internal or external, because event-driven autoscaling requires it
Move the queue into the Container Apps environment
questions.explanation: Functions on Container Apps requires ingress to be enabled for event-driven autoscaling; it can be internal when public exposure is not required.

questions.stem: A deployment omits the storage account because all business state lives in Cosmos DB. Why is the design invalid?
options: Container Apps requires Azure Files for every image
Every Function App on Container Apps still requires host storage for triggers, logs, and state
Cosmos DB cannot be accessed from Container Apps
Storage is needed only for HTTP triggers
questions.explanation: Functions host storage is mandatory even when business data is elsewhere because the Functions runtime uses it for host-level trigger, logging, and state responsibilities.

questions.stem: A team creates two active revisions of a queue-triggered Function using the same host storage and Service Bus queue, expecting a deterministic 90/10 canary. What is wrong with that expectation?
options: Pull-trigger revisions are competing consumers; use isolated event sources and storage or single-revision mode
Traffic weights automatically partition Service Bus messages
The queue must use sessions to enable HTTP traffic splitting
questions.explanation: HTTP traffic weights do not deterministically partition pull-based events. Concurrent revisions should isolate host storage and event sources unless competing consumption is explicitly intended.

questions.stem: A developer attempts to add a manual Service Bus KEDA rule in the portal, but the control is disabled. What explains the behavior?
options: Functions derives the KEDA rule from trigger configuration by default; custom rules require opting out with allowScalingRuleOverride
The app must run on a Dedicated profile
questions.explanation: The platform maps Functions trigger settings to KEDA scalers. Teams normally set replica bounds; they assume manual rule ownership only when explicitly overriding generated rules.

questions.stem: A Function must receive from Service Bus without a connection-string secret. Which configuration and role are appropriate?
options: Set ServiceBusConnection__fullyQualifiedNamespace and grant Azure Service Bus Data Receiver to the managed identity
Store RootManageSharedAccessKey in source and grant Reader
Set AzureWebJobsStorage to the Service Bus endpoint and grant Contributor
Use AcrPull on the Service Bus namespace
questions.explanation: An identity-based Service Bus binding uses the connection-name prefix plus __fullyQualifiedNamespace and requires the data-plane receiver role for trigger consumption.

questions.stem: A blob-triggered Function processes new blobs but does not scale automatically from blob arrivals on Container Apps. Which trigger design supports autoscaling?
options: A polling blob trigger with no event source
A Blob Storage trigger using Event Grid as its source
A timer that lists blobs every second
questions.explanation: Blob-trigger autoscaling on Functions hosted by Container Apps requires Event Grid as the source.

questions.stem: After idle scale-to-zero, the first HTTP request breaches the latency SLO but warm requests pass. Which response is most defensible?
options: Ignore the first request because scale-to-zero is always free
Measure cold-start distribution, then use minimum replicas or another hosting profile if the SLO cannot tolerate it
questions.explanation: Scale-to-zero creates a cold-start tradeoff. Use measured latency and workload economics to decide whether warm minimum replicas or another profile is required.

questions.stem: A poison Service Bus message repeatedly fails schema validation and consumes retries. What application behavior is required in addition to platform scaling?
options: Treat every failure as transient forever
Classify non-retryable input, preserve diagnostics, and use the queue's dead-letter policy while keeping side effects idempotent
Raise max replicas until the message succeeds
questions.explanation: Scaling cannot repair invalid input. The function must distinguish permanent from transient failures, support dead-letter operations, and tolerate at-least-once delivery.
